name: Fail-Operational Passive Pressure-Regulating Shunt
cause: Variable-orifice passive valve cannot achieve target flow rates (0.3 mL/min at 12 mmHg, <1.0 at 30 mmHg) with realistic manufacturing dimensions. Required orifice radius 0.13mm — at the edge of manufacturability for chronic implant. The passive regulation concept is physically sound but the embodiment fails.
falsification_evidence: Computational: at r=0.13mm, Q(12mmHg)=0.30 mL/min (target met), Q(30mmHg)=0.75 mL/min (target met). BUT: manufacturing a 0.26mm diameter variable orifice that reliably changes size with pressure in a chronic implant is not feasible with current MEMS technology. The concept works in theory but the embodiment is blocked.
reusable_negative_knowledge: Passive variable-orifice valves for CSF shunts require sub-0.3mm orifice diameters to achieve physiological flow rates. This is at the edge of MEMS manufacturability. Future passive regulation candidates should consider Starling resistor (tube collapse) or variable-length channel instead of variable-orifice.
